- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.00) or mixed, model underestimates; apply upward bias correction.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 3–5 days.
- If model shows strong mean reversion bias (e.g., forecasting back to historical mean after volatility), adjust for sentiment-driven momentum — if sentiment is bullish, allow continuation; if bearish, cap downward movement.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period price action (last 7–10 days); apply upward adjustment if sentiment is bullish or volatility is rising.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive within 3–5 days, model often lags; adjust forecast to reflect sentiment change within 2–3 days.
- Avoid over-reliance on recent 18-day history — sentiment and volatility context matter more than pure trend.
